course.title: Computer Graphics I
course.description: Documenting the projects and assignments completed for Computer Graphics I, including goals, process, results, and demos for each project.

projects.title: Homework 2 - First Rendering Algorithm
projects.summary: For homework2 I applied my first rendering algorithm in HTML and JavaScript.
projects.goals: The goal was to render a 3D cube by applying the pinhole camera perspective to create a 2D image. Additionally, provide moving camera views by key press.
projects.process: I applied simple 3D projection math using the camera vertices and cube vertices to display a cube.
projects.result: I learned how to render a cube and implement different camera movements within a canvas.

projects.title: Project 1 - Pinhole Camera, Rasterized Display
projects.summary: For Project1 I rasterized lines, pixels, and triangles by applying Computer Graphics Concepts that use vector math.
projects.goals: The goal for this project was to create a web application in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to develop a minigame using the canvas API and Computer Graphics concepts to implement a rasterized display in three different render levels.
projects.process: I designed a rasterized display with reusable block, diamond, and floor objects built once and instanced with their own position, scale, and color. Using pinhole camera projection, I implemented three rendering levels: canvas line-drawing, a rasterized 320x200 pixel display with a custom DDA line algorithm, and a triangle-rasterized level with a depth buffer and Lambertian shading. Along the way I handled near-plane clipping (line interpolation and the Sutherland-Hodgman algorithm), camera-relative object regeneration for an infinite floor, and bounding-box collision detection.
projects.result: I built a working trench-run minigame across three rendering levels: wireframe line drawing, a rasterized 320x200 pixel grid, and shaded triangle rasterization with a depth buffer. Along the way I learned how to solve real rendering problems firsthand, like fixing incorrect depth ordering by interpolating 1/z instead of z, clipping geometry against the near plane so the camera doesn't produce unreasonable coordinates behind it, and computing per-triangle shading from face normals and a light direction.
